deltas.description: Totalized-gradient algebraic interface is broader than source classical derivative assumptions.
deltas.evidence: The two new declarations intentionally omit C1/C2. The gradient is Lean totalized fderiv passed through the Riesz map. It is not a freely supplied vector field, but one must not identify it with an existing classical derivative at arbitrary points. Lessons explicitly state this and the global model premise. Source smooth functions are a specialization; this is not source-equivalent regularity.

deltas.description: Hilbert-space and signed-parameter domain extensions are explicitly disclosed.
deltas.evidence: Fresh elaborated statement, blind reconstruction and all candidate lesson assumptions agree on absent C1/C2 and real parameters.

deltas.description: The printed step condition omits the necessary nonnegative lower bound.
deltas.evidence: Same f with alpha=beta=1, z=0,x0=1,N=1,h=-1 satisfies exact PL and all printed source premises. The new gap is f(2)=2, but (1-alpha h)(f(1)-f(0))=1. Thus 2<=1 is false. For every h<0, (1-h)^2>(1-h).

deltas.description: No extra q>=0 assumption is needed because the supplied minimum resolves q<0.
deltas.evidence: For q<0, 0<=G(Tx)<=q G(x) and G(x)>=0 imply G(x)=0 for every x. Consequently both sides of the conclusion vanish for every N, including odd N; the proof never multiplies an inductive inequality by a negative q. This branch is nonempty: constant functions with sufficiently large alpha h satisfy the models.

repairs.proposed_change: Add h>=0 to the printed h<=1/beta restriction in Theorem3.6. Retain the original pinned source separately and preserve the local algebraic generalization.
repairs.reconstructed_statement: Let f:R^d->R be C2 and beta-smooth with beta>0, admit a global minimizer z, and satisfy ||grad f(x)||^2>=2alpha(f(x)-f(z)) for all x with alpha>0. For every step 0<=h<=1/beta, define T(x)=x-h grad f(x). For every x0 and N in the natural numbers, f(T^[N](x0))-f(z)<=(1-alpha h)^N(f(x0)-f(z)).
repairs.justification: Same f with alpha=beta=1, z=0,x0=1,N=1,h=-1 satisfies exact PL and all printed source premises. The new gap is f(2)=2, but (1-alpha h)(f(1)-f(0))=1. Thus 2<=1 is false. For every h<0, (1-h)^2>(1-h).
repairs.minimality_evidence: Only the lower bound h>=0 is added to the source step domain; h=0 remains valid. Source positive modulus/regularity/attained-minimum/PL premises are retained. No convexity or q>=0 assumption is added. Omitting the new lower bound admits the explicit quadratic counterexample.
repairs.reference_or_counterexample: Primary source https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3, Theorem3.6. Exact counterexample: Same f with alpha=beta=1, z=0,x0=1,N=1,h=-1 satisfies exact PL and all printed source premises. The new gap is f(2)=2, but (1-alpha h)(f(1)-f(0))=1. Thus 2<=1 is false. For every h<0, (1-h)^2>(1-h).

review_evidence: Accepted scoped source support for Theorem3.6 with explicit h>=0 and separately disclosed totalized-gradient, signed-modulus, Hilbert-space generalization. The literal negative-step source assertion and any automatic source repair acceptance are excluded. Entire current PL and imported shared Basic modules and bound lesson/provenance reviewed. Let G(x)=f(x)-f(z). IsMinOn gives G>=0 everywhere. Multiply 2alpha G(x)<=||gradient f(x)||^2 by h/2>=0 and combine shared descent to derive G(Tx)<=q G(x), q=1-alpha h. No convexity, sign of alpha or sign of beta is needed for this algebra. For q<0, 0<=G(Tx)<=q G(x) and G(x)>=0 imply G(x)=0 for every x. Consequently both sides of the conclusion vanish for every N, including odd N; the proof never multiplies an inductive inequality by a negative q. This branch is nonempty: constant functions with sufficiently large alpha h satisfy the models. Run artifact: /private/tmp/andi-pl-source-review-run-01.json
